The only surprises left in ownership are the good ones.

About Valet · The Why & The Who

Built because
nothing else was.

You didn't buy the car to manage a filing cabinet. You bought it for cold-start mornings, canyon light, and the people who get it. Somewhere between the price guides that don't know your car, the belt service that ambushes you, and the club you can never quite find, ownership turned into work.

Our mission is to make owning the cars you love as rewarding as driving them: know what every car is truly worth, see every mile and every dollar ahead, and keep your people one tap away.

The Money·The Maintenance·The People·Built by Owners·Est. Los Angeles

The Problem We Live With

01
Valuations without context
Price guides give you a directional number that shifts weekly and doesn't account for your specific car. Book values average a 30%+ discrepancy on collector-grade vehicles. Neither tells you where the value is heading or what's driving trends in your segment.
02
Maintenance as a black box
No forward-looking roadmap of what's due, when, and what it costs. Worse, no tool connects maintenance spend to value impact. A $4,200 belt service might protect $12,000 in appreciation, but owners have no visibility into that math.
03
No picture of true return
Insurance, storage, registration, fuel, detailing, scheduled and unscheduled service: it all adds up. But nothing aggregates carrying costs against appreciation to show the real net return. The difference between a smart hold and a money pit stays invisible.
04
The analog reality
Manila folders of printed receipts. Waiting for your mechanic to call. The dental appointment model applied to six-figure assets. That barely works for one car; it breaks completely at three, five, or ten.

Why Now

The collector market has institutional-grade money flowing through consumer-grade tools. Auction and sales data has finally become deep enough to price individual cars rather than categories. A new generation of enthusiasts runs their entire lives through software and expects the garage to follow. And the independent specialists who keep these cars alive want exactly the kind of qualified demand Valet routes to them. The window is open, and nobody has walked through it.

Who's Building It

Fig. 05 · The Collector
Johnny
CEO / Founder
Johnny is the collector in the room: Ferrari Club of America, Porsche Club of America, Hagerty Drivers Club, and a garage that runs from vintage Alfa Romeos and Porsches to modern Ferraris and Aston Martins. He's spent fifteen years building and scaling technology companies, most recently helping grow one from $10M to over $120M in revenue, and just as long treating collector cars as the investment assets they are: tracking comps, timing services, logging every dollar in and out. Valet is that discipline, finally made into software.
Fig. 06 · The Builder
Jens
CTO / Cofounder
Jens is the builder. He's the founder of Nettlio, his own AI agency, and the most senior platform engineer at Supernal AI, where he and Johnny met. He's spent his career shipping production systems that the country's leading transportation and financial services firms rely on every day. As CTO of Valet, he owns the full technical roadmap and architecture and leads a team of platform engineers building the perpetually growing vehicle database at the core of the product.

Our obsession with the cars. Fluency in them as assets. A proven record scaling technology companies. This is where it all harmonizes.
